questions.question: What window function assigns ranks with gaps for ties?
questions.explanation: RANK() assigns the same rank to ties but skips subsequent ranks, creating gaps.

questions.question: What window function assigns consecutive ranks for ties?
questions.explanation: DENSE_RANK() assigns the same rank to ties without skipping any rank numbers.

questions.question: What clause divides result sets into groups for window functions?
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY divides rows into groups, applying window functions separately to each partition.

questions.question: What function accesses data from a previous row in the result set?
questions.explanation: LAG() retrieves values from preceding rows without using self-joins.

questions.question: What function accesses data from a following row in the result set?
questions.explanation: LEAD() retrieves values from subsequent rows in the ordered result set.

questions.question: What function returns the first value in an ordered partition?
questions.explanation: FIRST_VALUE() gets the first value in the current window frame or partition.

questions.question: What function returns the last value in an ordered partition?
questions.explanation: LAST_VALUE() gets the last value in the current window frame or partition.

questions.question: What technique optimizes subqueries by caching results?
questions.explanation: Materialization stores subquery results in a temporary table to avoid repeated execution.

questions.question: What operator compares a value to any value in a subquery?
questions.explanation: ANY compares against at least one value in the subquery result; SOME is equivalent.

questions.question: What function divides rows into specified number of groups?
questions.explanation: NTILE() distributes rows into a specified number of approximately equal groups.

questions.question: Complete the SQL: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (______ AVG(salary) FROM employees);
questions.explanation: The subquery needs its own SELECT to compute the average salary for comparison.

questions.question: Complete: SELECT dept, COUNT(*) FROM emp GROUP BY dept ______ COUNT(*) > 5;
questions.explanation: HAVING filters on the aggregate COUNT(*); WHERE cannot reference aggregates after grouping.

questions.question: Complete: SELECT name, RANK() OVER (______ BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM emp;
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY restarts the ranking within each department.

questions.question: Which keyword must follow WITH to define a recursive CTE in standard SQL?
questions.explanation: WITH RECURSIVE defines a CTE that may reference itself to iterate over hierarchies.

questions.question: Complete: SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY id OFFSET 10 ROWS FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ______;
questions.explanation: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY is the standard SQL syntax for limiting returned rows.
